# Intake Brief — find-related: improve keyword relevance (IDF/title weighting)

## Problem statement

Keyword extraction in `find_related.py` is frequency-ranked and capped to the
top 8 (`MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS`), but raw frequency lets corpus-generic words
dominate, so `wl search` queries are built from terms that carry little signal
and the returned "related" items are often unrelated. Title terms and
distinctive domain terms are not weighted above generic body words.

## Users

- **Pi agents** running `/skill:find-related` during intake/plan/implement —
  they consume the "Related work (automated report)" section appended to work
  item descriptions and need genuinely related precedent.
- **Producers** reviewing work items — they spend time triaging spurious
  "related" links.

Example user stories:

- As a build agent, I want the related-work section for a find-related skill
  improvement to surface the skill's own prior reviews and keyword tests, so I
  don't re-read unrelated lint items.
- As a producer, I want to trust that at least the top-ranked related items
  are on-topic, so triage is fast.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9 ("Review find related skill"), at least 2 of the
      top 3 related work items are genuinely related to the find-related skill
      (manual reviewer judgement, documented in the work item).
- [ ] Keyword selection is deterministic across re-runs: identical input
      returns an identical keyword list (idempotency preserved; ties remain
      broken alphabetically).
- [ ] Distinctive domain terms outrank corpus-generic terms in the extracted
      keyword ordering (asserted by new unit tests; title tokens weight higher
      than body tokens; expanded project-generic stop-word list drops
      "work"/"item"/"report"/"review"/"skill" where they add no signal).
- [ ] Existing find-related unit tests pass or are updated only where they
      codify the old pure-frequency ordering; new tests assert the new ranking
      behaviour, including determinism and stop-word handling.
- [ ] No increase in runtime beyond the v3 bound: the per-keyword `wl search`
      subprocess count remains capped (≤ `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS`).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` ranking-heuristic tables,
      and README or wiki entries where relevant.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the v3 feedback-loop fix: the automated-report section is stripped
  from the description before extraction; no unbounded keyword growth.
- Conservative policy: prefer false negatives over false positives. A term is
  only a keyword if it adds genuine signal.
- `wl search` subprocess spawns are the dominant runtime cost (~0.4–0.5s each);
  keyword selection must stay within the existing capped fan-out. No new
  per-keyword subprocesses beyond the v3 cap. (True corpus-wide IDF via a
  dedicated per-term document-frequency pass would violate this cap.)
- Preserve report compactness (keyword lists per repo file capped at
  `MAX_KEYWORDS_PER_FILE`, `(+N more)` markers) and the deterministic
  tie-breaking (alphabetical) guarantee.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-boosting title terms** could let a generic title word (e.g. "review",
  "skill") dominate the keyword list and reproduce today's problem in a new
  form — mitigate by combining title boost *with* the project stop-word
  expansion, and assert in tests that a generic title word does not outrank a
  distinctive body term.
- **Aggressive stop-word expansion** can drop a genuinely distinguishing term
  (e.g. "report" distinguishing report-related skills). Conservative policy
  (prefer false negatives) accepts this; document any term added to
  `STOP_WORDS` in code comments with its rationale.
- **Regression risk in keyword tests**: `test_frequency_ordering_puts_descriptive_core_first`
  and several `test_find_related.py` keyword tests codify pure-frequency
  ordering; updates must preserve the deterministic/alphabetical-tie contract
  or they become flaky.
- **Scope creep**: sibling items SA-0MUG46YR2006URF4 (verbose keyword
  listing) and SA-0MUG4654N000DFLQ (runtime <5s parallelisation) touch the
  same script but are separate work — do not fold them into this item;
  coordinate only to avoid merge conflicts in `find_related.py`.

## Assumptions

- The wl search `score` field (BM25/hybrid) continues to rank the *returned*
  items; this item changes keyword *selection* only, unless the implementer
  demonstrates a re-ranking need in review.
- True corpus-wide IDF is unavailable without extra subprocesses; the
  title-boost + stop-word-list approach is accepted as the "or equivalent"
  permitted by the seed context.

## Existing state

- `extract_keywords(title, description)` concatenates `title` + description
  and returns unique tokens ordered by **descending raw frequency** (ties
  alphabetical), after stop-word/length/numeric filtering
  (`find_related.py:177–216`).
- Title tokens are counted identically to body tokens (the title is just
  prepended to the combined text), so a title's single occurrence carries no
  more weight than one body occurrence.
- `STOP_WORDS` is a general English list only; project-generic terms
  ("work", "item", "report", "review", "skill", "related", "find") are not
  excluded.
- `search_and_dedup` queries the top-8 frequency keywords, one `wl search`
  each, and ranks *returned* items by the `score` field — but the candidate
  set is fixed by keyword *selection*, so retrieval quality is bounded by
  extraction quality.
- **Live reproduction (this intake session, SA-0MUG46NJE003JOCD):** a
  `find_related.py` run returned 3 unrelated completed lint work items
  (`SA-0MS3ATYK1003IGR7`, `SA-0MS3ATYU5009Q3J8`, `SA-0MS3ATZ490094SSI` — all
  "Do not catch blind exception (BLE001)" findings against `find_related.py`)
  and audit docs as top repo matches — matched on generic words
  ("acceptance", "audit", "behaviour"). The searched top-8 keywords were
  `related, skill, find, terms, keyword, audit, frequency, generic`.
- Existing test `test_frequency_ordering_puts_descriptive_core_first`
  (`tests/test_find_related_v3.py:107`) codifies pure frequency ordering
  (`keywords[:3] == ["search", "optimize", "speed"]`) and will need to be
  updated/renamed to assert the new weighting.

## Desired change

- **Weight keywords** so distinctive domain terms outrank corpus-generic
  terms, using inverse-document-frequency (IDF) or an equivalent
  zero-extra-cost proxy, and boost title terms over body/description terms.
  Deliverable is an *ordering* change to `extract_keywords` (still
  deterministic, still capped at `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` for search)
  — mechanism options for the implementer:
  1. **Static title boost + expanded project stop-word list** (deterministic,
     zero subprocess cost; recommended as the baseline): multiply/weight title
     tokens; add project-generic terms to `STOP_WORDS`.
  2. **Result-set-size IDF proxy**: use the `count`/result-set size returned by
     the *existing* 8 `wl search` spawns — a generic term returns ~20 (cap),
     a distinctive term returns few. Zero extra subprocesses, but only
     available *after* the first sweep, so it best augments ordering/display
     rather than selecting the sweep. (True corpus IDF via direct worklog DB /
     FTS reads is explicitly **out of scope** — it bypasses the `wl` CLI as
     source of truth and couples the script to the DB schema.)
- **Expand `STOP_WORDS`** with project-generic terms that add no signal.
- The seed's optional **minimum relevance threshold** is deferred:
  implementation may drop a keyword with no results, but the related-items
  list keeps its soft top-3 cap (`MAX_WORK_ITEM_RESULTS`) — see Appendix Q2.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/find-related/scripts/find_related.py` — `extract_keywords`,
  `STOP_WORDS`, keyword-ordering logic (`MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` selection).
- `tests/test_find_related.py` — existing keyword unit tests
  (`test_keywords_from_title`, `test_keywords_excludes_common_stop_words`, …).
- `tests/test_find_related_v3.py` — `TestKeywordRankingAndNoise`,
  `TestExtractKeywordsSkipsReportSection`.
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — keyword-extraction description, ranking
  heuristics tables, `MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS` docs.

## Related work

### Potentially related work items

- **SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9** — "Review find related skill" (completed). The v3
  review that discovered this item; the acceptance basis for AC1.
- **SA-0MUG46YR2006URF4** — "find-related: verbose output lists all extracted
  keywords, not the searched subset" (open, same discovery). Sibling issue on
  `find_related.py` (diagnostics, not ranking). If both are implemented, the
  verbose line should reflect the *searched* subset.
- **SA-0MUG4654N000DFLQ** — "find-related: bring runtime back under the 5s
  target" (open, same discovery). Parallelises the 8 `wl search` calls;
  overlaps the runtime constraint — any keyword-selection change should stay
  agnostic to (and compatible with) that parallelisation.
- **SA-0MQ8MW73R001NSQZ** — "Unit tests for keyword extraction" (completed).
  Existing keyword-extraction coverage.
- **SA-0MQ8MWVXH004F63S** — "Worklog search and deduplication logic"
  (completed). `search_and_dedup`/ranking history.
- **SA-0MRPL5WLZ000JZ9V** — "Related Items is too broad" (completed). Prior
  relevance/compactness work on the same report; both items cap repo-file
  keyword lists, soft top-3 limits.

### Potentially related docs

- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — `### Ranking heuristics`, `### Configurable
  limits`, keywords decision-logic step 2.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` — find-related report usage in intake.

### Automated related-work report

A `find_related.py` run on this item during intake (2026-10) inserted a
"Related work (automated report)" section showing the current bug in action
(3 unrelated BLE001 lint items + audit docs); regenerated report should be
re-evaluated after this change as manual verification of AC1.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should 'IDF or equivalent' be implemented given the subprocess cap
  (true corpus wide document-frequency requires a per-term pass)?" — **OPEN
  QUESTION.** Recommended (deferred to developer under Constraints): static
  title boost + expanded project stop-word list, with the result-set-size
  proxy as an optional augmentation from the existing 8 spawns; a direct
  worklog DB/FTS read for true IDF is out of scope (bypasses `wl` CLI,
  couples to DB schema). Source: seed context ("or equivalent",
  "subprocess count remains capped") + code inspection of
  `extract_keywords`/`search_and_dedup` (title currently counted once like any
  body token).
- Q2: "Should a minimum relevance threshold be enforced (dropping weak items,
  potentially yielding an empty related list)?" — **OPEN QUESTION.**
  Recommended: defer; keep the soft top-3 cap (`MAX_WORK_ITEM_RESULTS`), drop
  only keywords with no results. Rationale: conservative policy prefers false
  negatives, but an always-empty report would break producer expectations
  built on the soft-cap behaviour. Source: seed context ("Optionally require
  a minimum relevance threshold") + existing `MAX_WORK_ITEM_RESULTS` soft-cap
  comment in `find_related.py`.
- Note: interactive interview skipped — seed context supplied problem,
  evidence, proposed improvement, ACs, and constraints; remaining choices are
  implementation-detail options recorded above for the producer to override
  at review.
data.title: find-related: improve keyword relevance (IDF/title weighting)

# Soft-deleted work items can be resurrected by status updates and re-dispatched

## Problem statement

A soft-deleted work item (one where `wl delete` has set `deletedBy`) can be resurrected via a status update, after which the downtime dispatcher re-selects it for dispatch. This caused the false-positive test-failure item SA-0MUJ14FQQ006R3PD to be worked twice after it had already been deleted.

## Users

- **Agent automation (Map, Build, etc.)**: agents rely on the downtime dispatcher to assign work and on soft-delete to permanently exclude items. Resurrection breaks this contract and wastes capacity.
- **Operator/Producer**: expects that a deleted work item will never re-appear in the dispatch queue or be worked by an agent.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **`wl update --status` refuses to change the status of a soft-deleted item.** The command checks `deletedBy` before accepting any status mutation, exits non-zero, and returns a clear error naming the deleted item.
2. **`StatusLifecycle.ensure_claimed` refuses to claim a soft-deleted item.** When `wl show` returns a non-empty `deletedBy`, `ensure_claimed` raises a `ClaimError` (or equivalent) instead of silently issuing a `wl update --status in-progress`. `require_claimed` also checks `deletedBy` in addition to status.
3. **The downtime dispatcher excludes soft-deleted items.** The worker filters out items where `deletedBy` is set (in addition to existing `status`-based filters) at the candidate-selection stage, before the Herdr list is consumed.
4. **All three guards are covered by automated tests.** Unit tests verify each refusal path; integration tests verify the dispatcher does not dispatch a soft-deleted item.

## Constraints

- The fix must be backward compatible: items already in flight at the time of the fix must not be affected.
- The `wl delete` command already sets `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`; this fix ensures those fields are respected everywhere they matter.
- Performance impact must be negligible — each guard is a single-field check on the work-item dict returned by `wl show` or `wl list`.
- The change spans two repositories: SorraAgents (`StatusLifecycle`) and ContextHub (Worklog CLI + herdr dispatcher). Each guard is implemented, built and tested in its own repository; no single worktree spans both.

## Existing state

- `wl delete` sets `deletedBy` on the work item but **may leave the status untouched** (e.g. `open`, `in_progress`, or `completed`). Source: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:766`.
- `StatusLifecycle.ensure_claimed` and `require_claimed` only check `status` — they do **not** check `deletedBy`. Source: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py:641-730`.
- The downtime dispatcher in ContextHub/herdr filters by `status === 'open'` or `status === 'blocked'` but does **not** filter by `deletedBy`. Source: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:6689, 6740`.
- `implement.py` already correctly skips soft-deleted children via `_is_terminal_child()`, which checks `deletedBy`. Source: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:761-780`.

## Desired change

Three independent guard points must be hardened:

1. **Worklog CLI**: `wl update --status` (and `wl update` generally) must reject mutations on items with non-empty `deletedBy`.
2. **Shared StatusLifecycle**: `require_claimed` and `ensure_claimed` must check `deletedBy` and refuse to operate on soft-deleted items.
3. **Downtime dispatcher**: the worker must filter out items where `deletedBy` is set, in addition to existing status filters.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `require_claimed`, `ensure_claimed` methods (SorraAgents)
- `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py` — unit tests for the new refusal paths (SorraAgents)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — reference for the `_is_terminal_child` pattern (SorraAgents)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — candidate selection and status filters (ContextHub)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — Worklog CLI `wl update` command implementation (ContextHub)

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJ14FQQ006R3PD** — the false-positive test-failure item that was resurrected (deletedBy set, then re-dispatched)
- **SA-0MUTWB8BA003J0V6** — `_is_terminal_child` correctly handles soft-deleted children in implement.py
- **SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9** — claim-invariant: actively worked => in_progress (related to StatusLifecycle design)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Some agents may have already issued `wl update --status` on soft-deleted items before this fix. Mitigation: the fix only prevents future mutations; no rollback needed.
- **Risk:** The downtime dispatcher filters may exist in multiple places (candidate selection, Herdr list grouping, offer computation). All filter paths must be updated.
- **Assumption:** `deletedBy` is always non-empty string when a work item is soft-deleted (never an empty string, whitespace, or null). This is verified by inspecting the `wl delete` implementation.
- **Risk:** Adding checks in StatusLifecycle may break agents that rely on silent re-claim. Mitigation: add tests for each agent workflow that uses `StatusLifecycle`.
- **Scope creep:** This fix does not address why `wl delete` may leave status unchanged — that is a separate hygiene issue.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should `wl delete` also set `status=deleted` to prevent resurrection?" — Answer: No. The current convention is that `wl delete` sets `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`; status is optional to change. This fix makes `deletedBy` the authoritative gate everywhere, which is cleaner. Source: design decision from this intake.
- Q: "Does `wl delete` always set `deletedBy`?" — Answer: Yes, per the `wl delete` command implementation in the Worklog CLI. Source: code inspection.
- Q: "What about imported work items with `deletedBy` set via `wl import`?" — Answer: The audit_runner already filters these. All three new guard points will catch them uniformly. Source: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:10769`.
data.title: Soft-deleted work items can be resurrected by status updates and re-dispatched

# Tune audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling to eliminate residual bounded-queue saturation

## Problem statement

The bounded priority queue (SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM) eliminated fail-fast audit
re-queueing (27 → 0), but under peak-day traffic **14 items still exhausted the
bounded wait and returned a `bounded-queue saturation` verdict** (latest live
metrics: 3 residual, down from 14 at evaluation time). Per
`docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md`, this is a **capacity/timeout
problem — not an idle-gate problem**: the configured concurrency ceilings are
lower than the host's real audit-slot capacity, so peak bursts queue beyond
what the timeout bound permits.

## Users

- **Operators** running the herdr downtime dispatcher: they expect audits to
  complete with real verdicts even during peak multi-agent traffic, not return
  an `unmet` "concurrency limit reached" verdict after a full wait.
- **Agent sessions** whose audits time out under saturation: today they burn a
  full bounded wait (90–115 s) and either retry later or leave items stuck in
  `in_review`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Right-sized ceilings:** `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` and/or
   `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS` defaults are raised to the host's real audit-slot
   capacity, *measured empirically* via the existing F7 harness
   (`skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` — the largest ceiling that keeps load
   < 16 on the 16-core host with no swap growth), informed by the 3-slot local
   LLM proxy pool.

2. **Timeout stays bash-window-safe:** `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` remains bounded
   (≈90–115 s) inside the parent bash-tool execution window (~120 s), so the
   SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL mid-wait-kill failure mode is not reintroduced.

3. **Zero residual saturation:** with N ≥ 3 concurrent audits against a busy
   host, **zero** `bounded-queue saturation` (or `host-wide saturation`)
   `unmet` verdicts are produced — all audits persist **real** verdicts
   (verification mirrors SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM AC1).

4. **No regression:** existing concurrency/queue tests keep passing —
   `test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`, `test_audit_queue_integration.py`,
   `test_audit_slot_lock_contention.py` — including the "timeout ≥ 0.1s < 5s
   bounded wait" behaviour and priority-ordering assertions; no test relies on
   the old default values being treated as constants.

5. **Documentation updated:** `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (fix the
   documented ceiling default — prose currently claims 2 while
   `process_semaphore.py` default is 5), `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
   (host-cap defaults), and the follow-up status in
   `docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md`.

6. **Full suite green:** the full project test suite passes with the changes
   (build → test → commit order per AGENTS.md).

## Constraints

- **Do NOT relax the herdr idle gate** (rejected in SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50); no
  ContextHub dispatcher change is in scope.
- Keep priority ordering (critical > high > medium > low; FIFO within tier)
  and the bounded-wait semantics of the shared priority queue unchanged.
- `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` must not exceed the parent bash-tool execution timeout
  (~120 s) unless the dispatch model changes — decoupling the wait from the
  bash-tool window is **out of scope**.
- The host's real capacity is bounded by the local LLM proxy
  (`session_slot_pool_size: 3` default) plus CPU/RAM headroom — the empirical
  F7 measurement is the source of truth.

## Existing state

| Knob | Default | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` | 90.0 s | `audit_runner.py:289-290` | Bounded queue+slot wait; 90s chosen to stay inside bash-tool ~120s window (SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL) |
| `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | 0.0 s | `audit_runner.py` | Per-attempt fail-fast inside the admission poll; total wait governed by queue timeout |
| `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (`DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS`) | 5 | `process_semaphore.py:75-76` | `_audit_semaphore_max_workers` precedence: CLI > env > 5 |
| `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS` | 3 | `audit_runner.py:250-251` | Host-wide ingress cap (`audit-host` semaphore) |
| `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | 90.0 s | `audit_runner.py:252-253` | Bounded wait for host ingress slot |
| Queue `max_depth` | 50 | `queue.py:94` | `QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH` override |

- Latest live metrics (2026-10-13): 771 admissions; bounded-queue saturation
  **3**; host-wide saturation 0; legacy fail-fast 0; max observed wait 599.8 s
  (historical, from a higher-override period).
- No deployment/pi/herdr env overrides for these knobs — **code defaults
  currently govern every project**. The herdr dispatcher sets only
  `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`.

## Desired change

Raise the audit concurrency ceilings to the **empirically measured** host
capacity (via `validate_fanout.py`, respecting the 3-slot proxy pool), keep
`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` bounded inside the bash-tool window, and update the
defaults + documentation so peak bursts drain through the queue instead of
timing out. Verify with N ≥ 3 concurrent audits against a busy host with zero
concurrency-limit `unmet` verdicts.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — ceiling/timeout defaults
  (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`, `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS_DEFAULT`,
  `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`), `_audit_queue_timeout()`,
  `_acquire_audit_slot()`, `_acquire_host_audit_slot()` (see ~line 3402,
  12468-12554)
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — `DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS` /
  `ENV_MAX_WORKERS` (`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`) ceiling
- `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` — F7 load-validation harness for
  empirical capacity measurement (mock pi, throwaway worklog)
- `skill/shared/audit_gate_metrics.py` — read-only metrics collector for
  verification (reports bounded-queue saturation counts)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — ceiling/timeout
  default tests (`test_default_ceiling_documented`,
  `test_default_queue_timeout_is_bounded_not_fail_fast`)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_queue_integration.py` — queue-wait and
  priority-ordering tests
- `skill/shared/tests/test_audit_slot_lock_contention.py` — lock-contention
  timeout tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — concurrency docs (fix stated default)
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — host-cap documentation
- `docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md` — evaluation + follow-up status

## Related work

- **SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50** (done) — idle-gate evaluation; recommended this
  follow-up (`discovered-from`); do not relax the herdr idle gate.
- **SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM** (done) — bounded priority queue integration; AC1
  north-star "zero concurrency-limit unmet verdicts" — this item's target.
- **SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L** (done) — shared bounded priority queue module.
- **SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5** (done) — batch drain mode.
- **SA-0MUV4C6RZ006GN5Z / SA-0MV0J0XXR008ZE6E** (done) — directory-lock
  timeout bounds.
- **SA-0MU7FD0YF0065EG9** (done) — stale queue-ticket saturation.
- **SA-0MU32T8SH001R8MZ** (done) — R4: no saturation abort of Phase 1 parent.
- **SA-0MSAEKOQE009TEB4** (done) — fan-out investigation (parent of F7).
- **SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF** — parent: multi-agent blocking on audits.
- **SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL** — prior art: 300s default killed audits mid-wait
  (origin of the bash-window constraint).
- **SA-0MSAWFTZX003T042** (done) — audit completion status semantics.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Raising ceilings raises concurrent suite runners** — mitigated by the
  F7-measured ceiling (load < 16, no swap growth) and the existing host-wide
  `audit-host` ingress cap; do not exceed measured capacity.
- **Cheap-proxy serialization** (01:00–10:00) already forces
  `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` in some windows — tuning must not fight that
  gate; verify in both modes.
- **Scope-creep risk:** decoupling the queue wait from the bash-tool window,
  relaxing the idle gate, or re-architecting dispatch is explicitly **out of
  scope**; record as linked follow-ups if discovered.
- **Assumption:** code-default changes are the correct mechanism since no
  deployment override exists today (operator confirmed).
- **Assumption:** the empirical F7 result, informed by the 3-slot proxy pool,
  is the definition of "the host's real audit slot capacity" (operator
  confirmed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Lever priority — raise concurrency ceilings vs raise timeout vs both?"
  — Answer (operator): "As you recommend" → **Option A: raise the concurrency
  ceilings and keep `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` bounded (~90–115 s) inside the
  bash-tool window.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Where the tuning lives — code defaults vs deployment env vs both?"
  — Answer (operator): "As you recommend" → **Option A: change the code
  defaults** (single source of truth; no deployment override exists).
  Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Capacity target definition — fixed number vs empirical F7 vs match
  proxy pool?" — Answer (operator): "As you recommend" → **Option B: measure
  empirically with `validate_fanout.py` (load < 16, no swap growth), informed
  by the 3-slot proxy pool.** Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L** – wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK (completed)
- **SA-0MUD8SBS2001P6G2** – Reproduce order-pollution deterministically (completed)
- **SA-0MUIUTJJS008W06Y** – plan-approval-gate skips checkpoint for t-shirt effort and Severe risk (open)

data.description:
# Add a tests-deleted-vs-added health metric and actively prune tests that no longer map to behaviour

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis currently reports test *additions* and *rewrites* but makes test *deletions* nearly invisible: whole-file deletions are hidden by the default diff filter, and there is no consolidated "tests added vs tests deleted vs net growth" figure per project or per test area. As a result the suite grows roughly 8:1 (82,381 added vs 9,968 deleted lines in modified test files, from the ContextHub analysis) with no health signal and no documented way to prune tests that no longer map to observable behaviour.

## Users

- **Maintainer of the pi agent infrastructure** — wants an honest, consolidated growth metric (added / deleted / modified / net growth) per project and per test area, in both the human report and JSON, so suite growth is visible at a glance without additional analysis.
- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants a trended growth signal over time (per calendar quarter) so regressions in net test growth are visible.
- **Agent enforcing testing policy** — wants a documented, repeatable workflow to identify and remove tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.

Example user stories:

- As a maintainer, I want the report to state, per project and per test area, exactly how many tests were added, deleted, modified, and the net growth, so I can see at a glance whether the suite is growing without bound.
- As a producer, I want the added/deleted/net-growth metric trended per calendar quarter, so regressions in test-suite growth are visible over time.
- As an agent, I want a documented review workflow for pruning tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, so pruning decisions rest on the metric plus explicit criteria rather than anecdote.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The analysis reports, per project and per test area: tests added, tests deleted, tests modified, and net growth, in the human report and JSON.
2. Whole-file test deletions are counted (diff filter includes `D`; rename detection applied so moves are not miscounted as deletions).
3. A documented review workflow describes how to identify and remove tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
4. The growth metric is trended over time **per calendar quarter** (derived from commit dates), so regressions are visible.
5. Tests cover the added/deleted accounting, including files deleted and re-added.
6. The metric is exposed by the reproducible `skill/test-churn` skill rather than as a standalone script.
7. At least one testing/validation criterion: the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the skill README/SKILL.md, and `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md`.

## Constraints

- Must live inside the existing `skill/test-churn` skill (AC6); no new standalone script and no ContextHub-specific paths.
- The metric must be derived deterministically from git history via the existing analyser entry point (`skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`), which is read-only against the analysed repository.
- Changes must not regress the corrected methodology implemented under `SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW` (real git name-status, documented rewrite-ratio denominators, distinct-commit temporal rates, whole-file deletion accounting).
- Growth trend granularity is calendar quarter derived from commit dates (operator decision Q2); release/tag-based grouping is out of scope.
- The item delivers metric + documented workflow only; the actual pruning pass is a follow-on item, not part of this work (operator decision Q3).
- Work item descriptions/comments in Markdown, UK English.

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` already computes: `modified_test_deletions`, `modified_test_additions`, `new_test_file_additions`, `deleted_test_files`, `deleted_test_lines`, and per-area `new_files` / `deleted_files` / `total_added` / `total_deleted` / `rewrites`.
- Whole-file deletion accounting exists (spans whole history, including test-only commits) and `--diff-filter=ADMRT` already includes `D`; AC2 is *mostly* satisfied but lacks explicit tests for delete-and-re-add.
- The temporal trend (`analyse_temporal_trends`) is currently **monthly rewrite-rate** only — there is no quarterly net-growth trend (AC4 is new work).
- No consolidated net-growth figure and no documented pruning workflow exist (AC1 headline and AC3 are new work).
- The skill's tests (`skill/test-churn/tests/`) cover deletion accounting in test-only commits and rename detection, but not file deleted and re-added (AC5 gap).

## Desired change

1. Add per-project and per-area accounting: **tests added, tests deleted, tests modified, net growth** (files and/or lines, consistently defined and documented) in `test_churn_data.json` and the human report.
2. Add a **quarterly net-growth trend** (per calendar quarter derived from commit dates) alongside or extending the existing temporal trend, in report and JSON.
3. Add a **documented review workflow** for pruning tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (in the skill SKILL.md and/or the dev reference doc).
4. Add tests covering added/deleted accounting including files deleted and re-added; update the skill reference documentation.

## Key Files

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` — add consolidated net-growth metric, quarterly growth trend, human-report + JSON sections.
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — document the new metric and the pruning review workflow (referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_churn_analysis.py` — tests for added/deleted accounting including delete-and-re-add.
- `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` — metric definitions, methodology and worked examples updated.

## Risks, assumptions & scope control

- **Assumption:** "net growth" is defined as additions minus deletions per project/area (files and lines reported separately), with the definitions documented so figures are unambiguous.
- **Assumption:** quarterly grouping is derived from commit dates on the analysed mainline; an empty quarter is reported as zero rather than omitted.
- **Risk:** renames are miscounted as delete+add if rename detection is misconfigured — mitigated by keeping `--diff-filter=ADMRT` + rename detection and covering moves in tests (existing `test_parse_name_status_handles_renames_and_plain_statuses`).
- **Risk:** the consolidated metric duplicates or contradicts existing fields, causing report confusion — mitigated by documenting the mapping from new fields to current ones in the reference doc.
- **Failure mode:** a file deleted and re-added in the same history could be under- or double-counted — covered explicitly by a new test (AC5).
- **Scope creep:** actually pruning dead tests from a suite is a distinct, higher-risk change; it is tracked as a follow-on work item (operator decision Q3), not part of this item.

## Related work

- Epic parent: `SA-0MV28WNFY009DF6Y` *Migrate test-churn / TDD-value analysis to SorraAgents and make reporting reproducible* (completed; recorded dependency).
- `SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW` *Fix test churn analysis status detection and rewrite-ratio denominator* (completed; methodology this work must not regress).
- `SA-0MV28WS5G004YNNS` *Create the reproducible test-churn reporting skill* (completed; the skill this metric extends).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — referenced by the pruning workflow (AC3).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What does 'per project' mean in AC1?" — Answer (operator, interactive reply): "A: the single analysed project's own report headings (project total + per-area breakdown)". Source: interactive reply in intake session. Research: existing analyser is single-project-root; multi-repo batch/aggregation is out of scope (potentially covered by `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` scheduled runs).
- Q2: "AC4 says 'per quarter or per release' — which granularity should the growth trend use?" — Answer (operator): "a: calendar quarter, derived from commit dates". Source: interactive reply. Research: quarters are universally derivable and deterministic; tag-based/release grouping is out of scope.
- Q3: "AC3 + title say 'actively prune'. Should this item actually remove dead tests now, or deliver metric + documented workflow with pruning as a follow-on?" — Answer (operator): "a: deliver metric + documented review workflow only; pruning is a follow-on item". Source: interactive reply. Research: removing suite tests is a distinct, higher-risk change needing its own evidence and review; it will be tracked separately as a follow-on work item.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0** – Migrate remaining raw-git test helpers to skill/shared/git_sandbox (open)
- **SA-0MS31SAM20004GTJ** – all actions should leave the status in a good state (completed)
- **SA-0MSHZ08OE0033049** – Remove AMPA documentation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, actively, add, added, also (+72 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, add, also, analysis, applied (+66 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: acceptance, actively, add, added, also (+60 more)
